claims.text: Superconducting behavior in HEAs is governed by local lattice distortions induced by compositional disorder.
Local lattice distortions enhance electron–phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling promotes superconducting pairing.
The initial HEA is a random solid solution of multiple metallic elements.
The initial HEA has minimal preexisting strain.
Changing cooling rate or annealing treatment can systematically vary local lattice distortion.
The proposed structural mediator is localized strain in atomic bonds associated with regions of compositional clustering.
Compositional disorder in HEAs creates local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions alter phonon spectra.
The altered phonon spectra enhance electron–phonon interactions.
Enhanced electron–phonon interactions facilitate Cooper-pair formation.
Samples with greater local lattice distortion will have a higher superconducting transition temperature than samples with minimized distortion.
Samples with greater local lattice distortion will have stronger electron–phonon coupling than samples with minimized distortion.
Annealing reduces local lattice strain in the proposed baseline samples.
The mechanism is expected to apply primarily to HEAs with significant compositional randomness.
The proposed explanation may not apply to simpler binary superconductors.
The proposed explanation may not apply when electron–electron correlations predominate.
Identically composed HEA batches processed under different cooling and annealing conditions provide the proposed controlled comparison.
The hypothesis is falsified if greater measured lattice distortion produces no statistically significant increase in both electron–phonon coupling and Tc relative to the annealed baseline.
